## Stability of CSTR Steady States {.cc}

Class 13 examines the stability of CSTR steady states and the parametric sensitivity of stable CSTR steady states. It shows how the transient response to a perturbation away from a steady state can be used to assess the stability of that steady state.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 13 you should...

* Know the definition of stable steady states, unstable steady states, parametric sensitivity
* Understand 
    * when a reactor is perturbed from a steady state it may return to that steady state, transition to different steady state, or go into sustained oscillations
    * if a reactor is perturbed from a steady state and does not return to it, that steady state is unstable
    * when an operating parameter of a CSTR operating at a *stable* steady state is changed slightly, the reactor outputs will change substantially if the starting steady state is parametrically sensitive.
* Be able to
    * identify unstable steady states, ignition points and extinction points using a plot of outlet versus feed temperature
    * determine the stability of a CSTR steady state by simulating the transient response to a small perturbation
    * assess parametric sensitivity by analyzing the transient response to small changes in steady-state operating parameters
